trust_principles: Deny by default and fail closed on missing, stale, ambiguous or conflicting authority.
Authentication proves a principal; it never selects tenant, workspace, role or capability.
Tenant and workspace authority are resolved exclusively by trusted server-side policy.
Every authorization decision is scoped to principal, action, resource, tenant, workspace, purpose, data class and source-rights state.
Roles are templates only; effective authority is the intersection of active bindings and explicit capabilities.
The browser, model output and worker payloads cannot grant or widen authority.
Row-level security is mandatory defence in depth and does not replace service-layer authorization.
Unknown data classification or source rights default to RESTRICTED.
Exports require explicit rights, purpose, destination, scope, manifest and auditable authorization.
Revocation and kill switches take precedence over cached decisions and in-flight convenience.
Break-glass access is exceptional, time-bounded, independently approved and fully audited.
Security events preserve non-repudiation without recording secrets or unnecessary personal data.

rules: Principal identifiers are opaque, immutable and unique within the trusted issuer.
Email addresses, display names and model-provided identifiers are never authorization keys.
Service and workload identities have no interactive session or organisation-owner privileges.
Credential rotation increments credential_version and invalidates older sessions.
A suspended, revoked or expired principal contributes zero capabilities.
Organisation, tenant and workspace are distinct resources and are never inferred from client-supplied identifiers.
Every tenant belongs to exactly one organisation; every workspace belongs to exactly one tenant.
Suspension of an organisation, tenant or workspace denies new access and export decisions.
Cross-tenant operations require an explicit platform capability and never reuse tenant-local roles.
Membership is explicit, time-bounded and independently revocable.
Invited, suspended, revoked or expired membership contributes zero capabilities.
Organisation membership does not imply access to every tenant or workspace.
Membership updates invalidate cached authorization decisions immediately.

separation_of_duties: For RESTRICTED or flagged data, export:create and export:approve must be exercised by different human principals.
A principal cannot approve its own break-glass grant.
SERVICE_WORKER cannot receive membership:manage, security:manage, rights:review, export:approve or billing:manage.
RIGHTS_STEWARD review cannot be substituted by a model, parser or source connector.
rules: Effective capabilities are the intersection of active principal, session, membership, role binding, resource scope and policy.
Client-supplied roles, capabilities, tenant IDs, workspace IDs and policy decisions are ignored.
Model output, tool output and worker payloads cannot create membership, role bindings or capabilities.
INDETERMINATE is treated as DENY at every enforcement point.
Resource non-disclosure returns the same external result for unknown and foreign resources.
Bearer credentials and session identifiers never appear in URLs, logs or browser-readable storage.
Privilege changes and credential rotation invalidate prior sessions.
Session context cannot override server-resolved organisation, tenant, workspace or capabilities.
Sensitive actions require recent authentication at the policy-defined assurance level.
RLS context is set with transaction-local server values after authorization and before data access.
Browser headers, query parameters, cookies and model output cannot set trusted database context.
Application roles do not own protected tables and do not possess BYPASSRLS.
SECURITY DEFINER functions pin search_path, validate scope and expose only the minimum operation.
Missing or malformed RLS context yields zero visible or mutable rows.
Classification is attached to source objects, evidence, claims, documents, exports and audit payloads.
Automated classification may propose but cannot lower an existing classification without human authority.
Secrets are never persisted in evidence, claims, exports or ordinary audit payloads.
Personal-data minimisation and purpose limitation apply independently from confidentiality.
The P02 source-rights snapshot is mandatory and version-pinned for every protected action.
Ambiguous, missing, expired, suspended, revoked or conflicting rights deny the affected action.
Technical accessibility never overrides rights, retention, attribution or redistribution restrictions.
Kill-switch activation invalidates cached allow decisions and blocks new materialisation or export.
Derived claims do not inherit export or redistribution rights unless explicitly authorised.
research:read never implies export:create or export:approve.
Every exported item must be enumerated in a deterministic manifest with provenance and rights snapshots.
Unknown destination, purpose, classification or rights yields REJECTED.
Sensitive exports use short-lived, audience-bound delivery and are not exposed through public object URLs.
Revoked or expired exports cannot be regenerated from stale approval.
Security audit events are append-only, hash-chained and independently queryable by authorised auditors.
Audit payloads exclude credentials, tokens, secrets and unnecessary personal content.
Denied and indeterminate decisions are logged with stable reason codes.
Audit readers cannot mutate security policy or operational resources.
Break-glass is unavailable to service principals, workloads and models.
The requester and approver must be distinct active human principals.
Break-glass never grants source-rights exceptions or export permission beyond existing rights.
Expiry or revocation removes authority immediately and invalidates active sessions.
